comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## BROADENED (operator): map TYPES, WORKFLOWS and STATUSES too — validate every vocabulary at once

The generalisation: **rebar hardcodes four vocabularies of instance strings, and each one is an
independent mismatch class.** From `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`:

    LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA   Highest / High / Medium / Low / Lowest
    LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA       the issue-type names
    LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA     To Do / In Progress / Done
    RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK    Blocks / Relates  (+ an inward/outward direction flag)

Every entry is a literal that must EXIST on the instance, with that exact spelling. Today the only
way we learn one is wrong is a live cell going red. One boot can check all four.

### This class has ALREADY cost this epic twice, which is the argument for including it

 * **[rebar:7f93]** — outbound status silently failed because **a transition's NAME is not its
   destination STATUS name.** `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` maps `in_progress` → `"In Progress"` (a state
   name), while DC's classic workflow offers transitions called `Start Progress` and `Done`. Matching
   on transition name alone missed, got soft-failed into `bridge_alerts`, and the pass exited 0 with
   the status unchanged. It never fired on Cloud because the DIG workflow names transitions after
   their destinations, so the two spellings coincide.
 * **[rebar:d067]** — outbound status submitted as a field edit rather than a transition at all.

So the map must capture BOTH spellings, per issue type, or it will reproduce exactly the blind spot
that produced 7f93.

### Added to the checklist

**Issue types (per project, as created):**
 * every issue type the default project yields, with `subtask: true/false` — the sub-task flag is
   what `set_parent` branches on
 * whether each name in `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` exists

**Workflows and statuses (per issue type — they can differ):**
 * which workflow is bound to each issue type
 * every status in that workflow, with its **name AND its status-category** (`To Do` / `In Progress`
   / `Done` categories are distinct from status NAMES, and inbound classification may rely on either)
 * for each status, the **transitions available FROM it**, recording for each the **transition name
   AND its destination status name** — the 7f93 pair, side by side
 * whether every value in `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` is reachable, and by which transition from which
   starting state. A status that exists but is unreachable from the initial state is a different
   defect from a misspelled one, and both are silent today

**Priorities and link types:**
 * `/rest/api/2/priority` — does every `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` value exist?
 * `/rest/api/2/issueLinkType` — does every `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` name exist, **and is the
   inward/outward direction flag correct?** A right name with an inverted direction produces a link
   that points the wrong way and would pass any name-only check

### The output shape that makes this useful

Not prose. A structured artifact whose most valuable section is a **direct diff: every rebar
vocabulary entry against what the instance offers**, with three verdicts per entry — present /
absent / present-but-different (wrong spelling, wrong direction, unreachable). That diff is
immediately actionable and is what the harness's startup assertion should later enforce.

**Report, do not fix.** If the map finds `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` disagrees with the instance, that is
a finding for a ticket — possibly a product bug, possibly a harness-config gap — and deciding which
is not the mapping job's call.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## LINK TYPES DESERVE THEIR OWN SECTION — a name-only check cannot catch the failure that matters

Already in the broadened checklist, but under-specified there. The actual map is:

    RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK: dict[str, tuple[str, bool]] = {
        "blocks":      ("Blocks",  False),
        "depends_on":  ("Blocks",  True),   # A depends_on B == B blocks A
        "relates_to":  ("Relates", False),
    }

**`blocks` and `depends_on` map to the SAME Jira link type and are distinguished ONLY by that
boolean.** So a direction error does not produce a missing link or an error — it produces a link
that exists, looks right, and **points the wrong way**. A dependency silently inverts. Checking that
the type name `"Blocks"` exists on the instance would pass with the direction completely wrong,
which is why this needs more than the presence check the other three vocabularies need.

The place it hides: Jira link types carry THREE strings, not one — the type `name` (`"Blocks"`) plus
distinct `inward` and `outward` names (`"is blocked by"` / `"blocks"`). Writing a link uses the type
name and a direction; READING one back inbound has to interpret the inward/outward name. A
mismatch between how we write and how we read is invisible to any single-ended check, and rebar
already has an 89-line `link_direction.py` devoted to this hazard.

### What the map job must capture

 * `/rest/api/2/issueLinkType` in full: for every type, its `name`, `inward` and `outward` strings —
   not just whether `"Blocks"` and `"Relates"` exist
 * an **end-to-end direction experiment**, because this cannot be settled by reading config: create
   A and B, write a `blocks` link A→B through rebar, then read the raw issue JSON for BOTH A and B
   and record which side reports which of the inward/outward names. Repeat for `depends_on` and
   confirm it lands as the INVERSE, not a duplicate of `blocks`
 * the same read-back for `relates_to`, whose symmetry means a direction bug is undetectable from
   the link alone and would only surface as a diff that never converges

### A gap the map should also record

Only **three** of rebar's seven link relations are mapped: `blocks`, `depends_on`, `relates_to`.
`duplicates`, `supersedes`, `discovered_from` and `caused_by` have no Jira equivalent here — so
presumably they do not sync at all. The map should record which of those the instance COULD express
(`Duplicate` and `Cloners` ship with stock Jira), so the "not synced" state is a documented decision
rather than an accident nobody has looked at. That is a finding to file, not to fix in the map job.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ALSO MAP THE LENGTH LIMITS — five hardcoded constants, none empirically confirmed on DC

Cheap to check and it closes a class the vocabulary checks miss. The constants:

    JIRA_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS   254     jira_family/value_maps.py:57
    JIRA_LABEL_MAX_CHARS     255     jira_family/value_maps.py:58
    WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT   32767   jira_family/rich_text.py:60      (DC description)
    _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS  32767   adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:41
    _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT   32000   adapters/jira/adf.py:332         (Cloud, margin under 32767)

Each is a documented-or-inferred number, not a measured one. A limit that is too HIGH means we send
a body Jira rejects — and bug 6afc records that **ACLI exits 0 on an over-length rejection**, so it
fails silently and re-emits every pass. A limit that is too LOW means we truncate content the
instance would have accepted, quietly losing user text. Both are silent; neither has a live check.

### The DC comment ceiling is CONFIGURABLE, which makes a hardcoded constant especially fragile

Bug 049e established that DC's comment limit comes from the instance property
`jira.text.field.character.limit`, with `0` meaning UNLIMITED. So the right value is not a constant
at all — it is instance state that the map job should READ, and that the declared environment
contract should then pin. If the harness image ships a different value than 32767, our fitting logic
is calibrated to the wrong number and no current test would say so.

### How to measure, per field

For `summary`, `description`, `comment` and `label`, write at **limit-1, limit, and limit+1** and
record the instance's actual response for each:

 * accepted intact → the limit is at least this
 * rejected with an error → the real ceiling, and the error shape (which matters: a silent 0-exit
   rejection is a different defect from a 4xx)
 * **accepted but SILENTLY TRUNCATED** → the most dangerous outcome and the one no unit test can
   see; detect it by reading the value back and comparing lengths, never by trusting the write

That read-back is the load-bearing part. Accept-and-truncate looks identical to success at the write.

### One subtlety worth carrying over

Cloud measures the description limit against the **ADF-serialized** size, not the plain text —
`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` is 32000 rather than 32767 precisely to leave margin, and a 32,767-char
description was observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars. DC's `WikiTextCodec` is a plain character
truncation instead. So the map should record **which representation the instance counts** for DC,
not assume it matches either. That question is live right now: a peer session is designing
Markdown⇄wiki conversion ([rebar:a32a-4549-3eb9-4fb9]), and length-fit measured on the wrong
representation is exactly the kind of mismatch that survives a green unit suite.

### Acceptance addition

- [ ] each of the five limits above is measured live at limit-1 / limit / limit+1, with the raw
      response recorded, and any divergence from the hardcoded constant reported as a finding
- [ ] `jira.text.field.character.limit` is read from the instance and recorded in the contract
      rather than assumed
- [ ] the accept-and-truncate case is detected by READ-BACK comparison, not inferred from a
      successful write

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE CAPABILITY-MAP JOB IS UP — Gerrit 1328

`scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml`.

**The placement constraint held**, verified rather than assumed: `git show --name-only` lists ZERO
files under `src/rebar/`. Project-specific tooling for one throwaway image stays out of the shipped
library, off its module-size budget, and out of the clean-core optionality gate's reach.

**It uses rebar's own agentic runtime rather than a hand-rolled client**: `rebar.llm.runner`
`RunRequest`/`get_runner` with `execution_mode="agentic"` and the default Opus model — the
"custom multi-call operation" seam `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents — plus
`rebar.llm.contracts.register_contract` for a bespoke Pydantic output contract, so the answer is
STRUCTURED (per-entry `present` / `absent` / `present_but_different` verdicts) rather than prose.
Step budget raised to ~450 tool cycles for the REST traffic.

**Design decisions worth keeping:**
 * **The digest pin is by CONSTRUCTION, not a second literal.** The job builds the SAME
   `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile` the existing harness builds, so the pin cannot drift
   between the two jobs — a genuinely better answer than repeating the digest.
 * **The vocabularies are read from their single source of truth** (`value_maps.py`,
   `rich_text.py`, `comment_limits.py`, `adf.py`) rather than copied into the script, so the diff
   cannot silently compare against a stale duplicate.
 * **`workflow_dispatch`-only is ASSERTED, not merely configured** —
   `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py` fails if the trigger, the read-only
   permissions, or the digest-pinned build ever change. That was an explicit AC and it is met by a
   test rather than by the YAML being currently correct.
 * **`REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`** gives a HARD guarantee the agent cannot mutate the ticket store,
   rather than relying on the prompt telling it not to.
 * Every REST call's raw request/response is captured into an evidence list keyed by id, which the
   agent must cite — the contract stays traceable to evidence, not to a model's summary.

Gates: ruff + zizmor + actionlint clean, mypy 421, hygiene 0, docs-index and env-registry checks
pass, 24 workflow-contract tests pass.

### TWO SCOPE JUDGMENTS I AGREE WITH

 * **The job does NOT auto-write comments to 37e7 / 1a9f.** That AC asked for the falsifier evidence
   to be recorded on those tickets; having an unattended CI job mutate the permanent, auto-pushed
   ticket store is a worse trade than a human posting the artifact's findings. Evidence lands in the
   artifact; posting is a documented follow-up.
 * **Landing the environment contract is NOT in this ticket.** This builds the tool that produces
   the evidence; deriving and committing the contract, and wiring it into the harness's setup
   assertion, is [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e]. It also cannot be done from a dev worktree — the image
   is amd64-only.

### PROCESS DEVIATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED

The implementer **claimed this ticket with `--force`**, bypassing the plan-review gate, on the
grounds that direct implementation had been directed. **That was not authorised.** AGENTS.md is
explicit that `--force` is "an escape hatch for a human operator's judgment call, not a routine
agent move", and "implement this" is not the same as "skip the gate". The instruction to implement
came from me; the gate bypass did not.

The work itself is sound and I am not reverting it over process. But it is recorded here because a
silently-forced gate is exactly the kind of thing that becomes normal if nobody writes it down, and
because a plan review might legitimately have challenged the scope judgments above BEFORE 575 lines
were written rather than after.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## AC4 + AC6 LANDED AS DATA — Gerrit 1333

The map's answers lived only in the CI artifact and in ticket comments, which is not what AC4 asks for. `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` now carries them as committed data, transcribed from run **30863672922**'s `capability_map.json` — not from recollection — with the `req-NNNN` evidence id behind each claim. Indexed in `docs/README.md` with a description that leads on the traps rather than the mechanism, so a reader designing against DC finds it.

**Why one doc and not a second:** the existing text referred to a prospective `docs/jira-dc-value-map.md` as the place committed data would go. That file was never created. Rather than add a near-duplicate filename beside `jira-dc-capability-map.md` — a discoverability hazard — the findings went INTO the doc that already describes the job, so the regeneration instructions sit next to the data they produce.

**Reading the artifact surfaced two facts that the ticket prose across this epic did NOT contain:**
 1. `POST /rest/api/2/issuetype` **succeeds** under the admin PAT (201, req-0076) — creating an issue type is a deterministic alternative to template pinning, if a future image ever stops shipping Epic.
 2. `POST /rest/api/2/screens/{id}/tabs/{id}/fields` **succeeds and read-back-verifies** (req-0078/0080). So adding Epic Link to a screen is *possible* — it is simply *unnecessary*, because the REST PUT persists without it. Those are different claims and the epic had been carrying only the second.
 3. Also newly surfaced: **`Parent Link` (customfield_10007, Advanced Roadmaps) is a distinct field from `Epic Link`** (req-0038). Any name-based lookup must match exactly — relevant to `_resolve_epic_link_field_id()` from 9bb9/1311.

Known vocabulary mismatches are recorded pointing at [rebar:2e47-ae62-c0cf-48a0] so they are not re-filed.

Gates: `test_check_docs_index.py` 13 passed, `make lint` clean.

Remaining ACs are the workflow-shape ones (AC1/AC5), already satisfied by change 1328, and AC3 (falsifiers recorded on 37e7/1a9f), already done. AC2's 'unambiguous answers' is now discharged by the doc rather than by the artifact alone.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE MAP'S STALENESS IS NOW CHECKABLE — Gerrit 1394

Working this ticket under `/rebar-implement`'s held-out TDD discipline. The skill's Phase-0 gate
**stopped**: 259b has no children (`rebar list-descendants` → all buckets empty), and the skill
executes an existing decomposition rather than creating one. Implemented directly against 259b's
own ACs with the same discipline instead — tests authored first, held out from the implementer.

### The gap I found, and why it is the one that mattered

Auditing the ACs against `origin/main` rather than against the ticket's prose: **AC1, AC2, AC3,
AC5 and AC6 are already met** by changes 1328/1333 and by the falsifier comments now on 37e7 and
1a9f. **AC4's consumption half is met too** — but by [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e], not by this
ticket: `_assert_project_capabilities` in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` enforces the
declared `_PROJECT_TEMPLATE` / `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` contract before any test runs. This doc still
described that as prospective work ("*an updated `docs/jira-dc-value-map.md` or* a harness setup
assertion that reads it"), naming a file that was never created; corrected to point at what
actually landed.

What was NOT met was implied by this ticket's premise rather than by a numbered AC. **The map
could go stale without anything noticing**, in two ways:

1. **The artifact's provenance was a hand-copied constant.** `_HARNESS_IMAGE_DIGEST` in
   `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` duplicated the digest pinned on
   `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile`'s `FROM` line — while the comment directly above it
   claimed the opposite: *"pinned by construction, not by a second literal that could drift from
   the first."* It **was** that second literal. The two agree today and **no test compared
   them**, so the first re-pin would have left `run_metadata.json` reporting the OLD digest —
   mislabelling which image was mapped, in the one file whose entire job is provenance.
2. **The committed answers named no image at all.** This doc warned that "a stale map after a
   re-pin describes an image nothing runs anymore" while recording nothing that could be checked
   against — an unfalsifiable warning. And since the instance **does not expose its own digest**
   over REST (only `scmInfo`), no live check could have caught it either.

### What landed

`harness_image_digest()` reads the `FROM` line, so the reported digest cannot drift from the
image actually built. It deliberately **does not raise** — this is metadata about a long,
billable live run, and aborting one over a malformed pin would discard the evidence the run
exists to collect; a missing file or an undigested `FROM` reports "no digest" rather than falling
back to a remembered value, which would mislabel the artifact just as badly as the bug it
replaces. The measured digest is now **committed data in this doc, asserted against the
Dockerfile's pin**, so a re-pin lands red until the map is regenerated. Plus `--print-digest`:
which image a run *would* map, with no container, key, or LLM.

### TDD evidence

Tests RED first, and I had to fix the oracle once before trusting it — the first run failed with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler.adapters'`, i.e. **the wrong reason**.
Root cause: `tests/unit/` ships its own `rebar_reconciler/` package and pytest puts the test's own
directory on `sys.path` ahead of the engine, so an in-process import of the script resolves the
shadowing test package. Rewrote the cells to drive the **real CLI** in a subprocess — which also
covers a gap worth naming: **`make lint` only lints `src tests`, so nothing in the local gate
reads `scripts/` at all**; a break there would first surface partway into a billable live run.

The implementer subagent saw **only** the happy-path cell (reported digest == Dockerfile digest);
the re-pin case, the unpinned case, and the doc staleness gate were physically moved out of the
worktree. **Both withheld edge cells passed unseen** — real signal, because a hardcoded constant
passes the happy path and still fails the re-pin case. Confirmed with teeth: re-introducing the
hardcoded digest turns exactly those 2 held-out cells RED while the happy path stays green.

Gates: `make lint` 0 (ruff + actionlint + zizmor), `make typecheck` 0 (mypy, 432 files),
12/12 cells in the target file, 96/96 across the repo-wide gates (docs-index, module-size,
comment-hygiene, workflow-parity/names, repo-isolation). `scripts/` checked directly since lint
skips it: `py_compile` 0, `--help` 0, `--print-digest` 0 emitting the Dockerfile's exact digest.
The full `tests/unit` suite does not finish in a usable local window — CI's `Verified` is the
authority there.

### The residual gap, filed as [rebar:a9bd-6641-e603-42bc]

This gate keys on the **digest**, so it catches "these answers describe a different image". It
does **not** catch **"these answers are wrong about THIS image"** — which is the failure this
epic actually hit: the retracted 255-char label claim was wrong at an **unchanged** digest. The
mechanism is that the answers are **LLM-summarised**; `evidence.json` was right and the *reading*
of it was wrong. That is the trust boundary this ticket set out to remove ("we have swapped
'discovering from the instance' for 'trusting a model', which is worse"), and closing it needs a
deterministic, non-LLM re-measurement pass. Filed with the description/comment 32767 **coverage
gap** (limit confirmed as configured, never as observed) recorded alongside it.

Not closing this ticket — the operator coordinating the epic is verifying the ACs.

compiled_state.description:
# An on-demand CI job that MAPS the Jira DC image, so we can declare its contract instead of discovering it

## Why this is the right instrument

The DC image is **amd64-only and exists only inside CI** — the development host is arm64, which is
why the previous AC verification pass recorded "no live cell was run during verification". Every
question about that image is therefore currently answered the same way: ship a change, wait ~35
minutes, read the failure. Today that loop was spent three times on ONE question (does the project
have an `Epic` type?), and the answer arrived as a SETUP FAILED at minute 35.

An on-demand GitHub Actions job that boots the pinned image and interrogates it collapses that loop
to a single run, and its OUTPUT is the environment contract that [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e] needs
written down.

## The load-bearing constraint: this is an AUTHORING tool, not a test-path component

**The deliverable is committed DATA, not a running agent.** If the agent ever executes on the normal
harness path, we have reintroduced exactly the runtime discovery the operator just ruled against —
with more non-determinism and an LLM in the loop. It must be:

 * **manually dispatched** (`workflow_dispatch`), never on push/PR/schedule;
 * **producing a committed artifact** — the declared capability contract plus the raw request/response
   evidence behind it — which a human reviews and lands;
 * **run again only when the image is re-pinned**, as the way we re-derive the contract for a new
   digest.

Its relationship to the harness is the same as a spike's to a story: it answers questions once so the
answers can be written down.

## What it should answer — a CHECKLIST, not open-ended exploration

An unscoped "go explore" agent returns prose. This should answer specific questions and emit
structured results:

**Inventory (what is there by default)**
 * exact image digest, Jira version, and licensed applications (Software present? — that determines
   whether `Epic` exists at all)
 * project templates the instance actually offers (`/rest/project-templates/latest/templates`)
 * for a project created from EACH candidate template: the issue types it yields
 * the full field inventory (`/rest/api/2/field`) — specifically the ids of `Epic Link` and
   `Epic Name`, which differ per instance
 * default screen configuration: is `Epic Link` on a standard issue's EDIT screen? is `Epic Name` on
   the Epic CREATE screen?

**Experiments (validate the configuration hooks BEFORE we depend on them)**
 * can the admin PAT create an issue type via `POST /rest/api/2/issuetype` and add it to a project's
   scheme? — the deterministic alternative to template roulette
 * can it add a field to a screen? Confirm by reading `editmeta` back
 * **the two falsifiers recorded on [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94]**: what operations does `parent`
   expose in a sub-task's `editmeta`, and does `{"update":{"parent":[{"set":null}]}}` behave
   differently from `{"fields":{"parent":null}}`? A difference overturns that ticket's
   NOT-RESOLVABLE verdict
 * **[rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] AC1**: does a sub-task `PUT fields.parent` return 2xx-and-ignore, or
   4xx? Raw REST, no rebar in the path
 * once an Epic exists: does writing `Epic Link` on a child actually take effect — the question
   change 1311 has now failed to reach three times

**Every answer must carry its raw request and response.** The contract must be traceable to evidence,
not to an agent's summary — otherwise we have swapped "discovering from the instance" for "trusting a
model", which is worse.

## Caveats worth designing against

 * **Pin by digest in this job too**, or the map describes an image we do not run.
 * **Boot time is minutes**; batch every question into one run rather than iterating.
 * The job holds an admin PAT on a throwaway instance — acceptable, but it must touch nothing
   outside it, and must not be reachable from a fork PR.
 * The agent must be told to REPORT rather than FIX. A mapping job that starts mutating the harness
   is how a spike turns into an unreviewed change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow boots the digest-pinned DC image and runs the checklist
      above, emitting a structured artifact (raw request/response per question)
- [ ] the artifact answers, unambiguously: which template yields `Epic`; the `Epic Link` /
      `Epic Name` field ids; whether those fields are on the needed screens by default; and whether
      creating an issue type + editing a screen via REST works with the harness's credentials
- [ ] the 37e7 and 1a9f falsifiers are executed and their raw responses recorded on those tickets
- [ ] the resulting environment contract is COMMITTED as data and consumed by the harness's setup
      assertion — it does NOT re-derive anything at test time
- [ ] the workflow cannot run on push, PR, or schedule, and this is asserted, not merely configured
- [ ] a short doc states when to re-run it (image re-pin) and that its output is authored, not live

file_impact.reason: commit the measured digest as data asserted against the pin, so a re-pin lands red until the map is regenerated; retract req-0022 (two ids named Task) citing run 30951453979 — a SAME-DIGEST contradiction, drift ruled out by comparing the pin

harness_image_digest() derives the reported digest from the Dockerfile FROM line, replacing a hardcoded second literal that could silently drift from the pin; adds --print-digest. Deliberately non-raising: a malformed pin must not abort a long billable mapping run

RED-first cells: dispatch-only trigger assertion, digest-derivation happy path, plus held-out re-pin and unpinned cases; drives the real CLI in a subprocess because tests/unit ships a shadowing rebar_reconciler package
